title: You can find any number from 1 to a million in just 20 guesses
body: If someone only answers “higher” or “lower”, always guess the middle of the remaining range. Each guess throws away half the possibilities, and halving a million 20 times leaves a single number, because 2 to the power of 20 is 1,048,576. This is binary search, and it is why a computer can find an entry in a sorted list of a billion items in about 30 steps.

slides.heading: Try it yourself
slides.text: Picking from 1 to 100? Guess 50, then 25 or 75, and keep halving. You never need more than 7 guesses, because 2 to the power of 7 is 128.

slides.heading: The catch
slides.text: It only works on sorted data. In an unsorted list you must check items one by one, which for a million items can take a million steps.

slides.heading: Easy to get wrong
slides.text: When Jon Bentley set it as a task, about 90% of professional programmers failed to write a correct version. Java’s library version hid a bug for over nine years.
